method: Web research 2026-10-15 from search-engine summaries of the cited pages (pages not opened directly).
overview: ERM (Environmental Resources Management) describes itself as the world's largest pure-play sustainability consultancy, with 8,200+ consultants in 150+ locations, advising companies on sustainability strategy, reporting, climate, environmental compliance, health and safety, and social impact.
service_lines: ESG due diligence (via ERM's sustainability institute and practices)

differentiators.text: Sustainability is the whole business, not one practice inside a generalist firm; the scale claim ('largest pure-play') is ERM's own.
differentiators.significance: Directly matches your strongest proof point (CDP/EcoVadis reporting, ESG RFPs).

early_career.text: Entry-level 'Consulting Associate, Sustainability' roles (Manhattan among the offices) support corporate sustainability strategy, materiality assessments and sustainability reports; ERM's early-careers page stresses hands-on work from day one.
early_career.significance: Day-to-day work maps closely to your GDI internship. Some postings ask 0-3 years.

early_career.text: A full-time graduate pathway (Compass Program) exists for associate consultants.
early_career.significance: A structured entry program, though posted for a different office.

tradeoffs.text: Much of ERM's work is technical (environmental compliance, permitting, health and safety) rather than strategy; strategy-and-reporting roles are a subset.
tradeoffs.significance: Check that the posting is in corporate sustainability, not field or compliance work.

unknowns: US benefits, leave and flexibility policies.
Pay relative to generalist consulting firms.
